claim: Directly incorporating a calibration objective (e.g., Brier/log-score term) into the same RLVR optimization target as accuracy creates a fundamental gradient conflict: the accuracy gradient and calibration gradient can point in opposing directions.
stance_target: feasibility of joint accuracy+calibration RL objectives (relevant to any DPRC RL/SFT training design)
scope_conditions: RLVR (reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards) training of reasoning LLMs
quoted_support: DCPO's fix is to systematically DECOUPLE the reasoning (accuracy) and calibration objectives (e.g., separate optimization steps/heads rather than a single summed reward).

claim: DCPO uses block-wise verbalized confidence rollout and decoupled advantage estimation, integrating instance-level and group-level signals, to preserve GRPO-level accuracy while achieving the best calibration performance among compared methods.
scope_conditions: reasoning LLMs trained with RLVR; general reasoning tasks, scalar per-response confidence
quoted_support: Extensive experiments demonstrate that DCPO not only preserves accuracy on par with GRPO but also achieves the best calibration performance and substantially mitigates the over-confidence issue.

claim: DCPO's calibration granularity is a single scalar confidence per full response/rollout, not per-requirement or per-test-case, and its evaluated domain is general RLVR reasoning rather than code generation with unit-test structure.
stance_target: DPRC's differentiation from DCPO on granularity and domain axes
scope_conditions: comparison of DCPO scope vs DPRC per-requirement code confidence
quoted_support: DCPO. THEORETICAL result directly relevant to design of any train-time calibration objective: proves that directly incorporating a calibration objective... into the same RLVR optimization target as accuracy creates a FUNDAMENTAL GRADIENT CONFLICT
